text:
Maya: Sharing a tiny toolkit for cross-functional OKRs and short peer-feedback prompts. Designed for fast alignment + low-friction 1:1 copy-paste.

Claire: omg this is what I needed for the Payments x Infra project. pasteable examples please.

Maya: yup. two parts: 1) cross-functional OKR skeleton + alignment note, 2) peer feedback micro-prompts for calibration and reviews. keep everything 1-2 lines.

Sam: Quick Q  how do we score cross-team KRs in calibration? different teams have different baselines.

Maya: propose: score by Business Impact (H/M/L) + Dependency Risk (H/M/L) + Likelihood (0-100%). capture a single rationale sentence. We collect these in the calibration sheet.

people-ops-bot: Template uploaded: https://internal.redwood/hr/xf-okr-feedback-toolkit (use "XF-OKR Kit v1") :white_check_mark:

Maya: Cross-functional OKR skeleton (paste into doc):
```
Objective: Launch unified billing flow to reduce customer billing errors and improve recovery rate.
Why it matters: prevents revenue leakage and reduces Ops support load.
KR1 (Product/Eng): Reduce billing error rate from 2.1% to <=0.5% in production by end of Q.
KR2 (Payments/Ops): Automate recovery for top 3 error classes; achieve 70% automated recovery rate.
Alignment note: Supports Revenue Reliability OKR (reduce churn from billing issues).
Impact/Dependency/Likelihood: High / Medium / 65% (explain: requires payments API flags + Ops runbook).
Owner(s): Product (Claire) + Eng (Sam) + Payments (Diego).
```

Diego: Love the Owner line. helps with triage.

Maya: Peer feedback micro-prompts (5 lines max) (copy into review form or ping):
```
1) "What progress or outcome from X did you notice that changed how you work with this person?"
2) "Where did they unblock cross-team work effectively? Any example?"
3) "One skill they should grow next quarter to increase impact: (short suggestion)"
4) "If you were me (their manager), one change you'd prioritize to boost their output?"
5) "Any risks or blockers they should be aware of going forward?" 
```

Claire: Those prompts are great, shorter than our old survey.

Sam: Can we get a short script managers can use to ask for upward feedback in 1:1s? I always over-explain.

Maya: Two-liner for managers to request upward feedback:

"Hi [Name], quick favor: can you share 2 sentences on (a) one thing I should keep doing and (b) one thing I should stop or change? Your candid note helps me support you better. Thanks!"

Diego: Any guidance for writing self-review bullets tied to KRs? Engineers hate fluff.

Maya: Self-review cheat: Use Result / Your Role / Evidence metric. One line per bullet. Example:
```
- Result: Reduced billing error rate on stripe-connector by 0.9pp. Role: Owned rollout and test harness. Evidence: Deployed canary + monitoring dashboard (link) and tracked p95 error rate weekly.
```

Sam: Nice. Also need a tiny onboarding blurb for new managers about calibration meeting format.

Maya: Calibration meeting 30m micro-agenda (paste):
```
- 5m: Quick primer + scoring rubric reminder (Impact/Dependency/Likelihood).
- 15m: Review 6-8 cross-team OKRs (2m each) with owner rationale line.
- 8m: Flag 2 items for escalation or resource rebalancing.
- 2m: Action items & owners.
```
